title: Implement fixed 60 Hz presentation and overload clock policy
requires: Any development host; access to current API, schedule and qualification records
scope: Implement the shared Gallery/client tick clock and previous/current-state interpolation contract, not domain solver changes. Follow docs/roadmap/F8-REALTIME-60HZ.md; preserve legacy-profile evidence and do not expand advertised interaction modes.
acceptance: Clock tests cover 30/60/90/120/144 Hz and jitter: at most one dt=1/60 tick per render callback, interpolation above 60, half-speed simulation at sustained 30, no catch-up or enlarged dt.
Specify and test presentation latency, orientation interpolation, spawn/removal/topology changes, resets, input/kinematic sampling, pause/background/resume and unavailable GPU snapshots.
Remove the new profile's 240-substeps-per-second policy; version any replacement of legacy behavior explicitly. Rendering must not require per-frame CPU physics readback.
Report simulation-to-wall-clock rate and interpolation alpha; slow-motion cannot masquerade as meeting a 60 Hz performance budget.

Focused ctest: 3 passed, session-clock skipped because this host exposes no Vulkan physical device; no physical-device or performance claim.
PASS: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/roadmap -p test_*.py; Python 3.11.2 on thomas-laptop: 72/72 passed.

REVIEWABLE CONTRACT: docs/roadmap/F8-04-PRESENTATION-CLOCK.md specifies explicit legacy/realtime versioning, one-tick latency, identity/topology/reset/lifecycle behavior, input sampling, unavailable GPU snapshots, and simulation/wall versus frame-performance reporting.
